title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 12/27 — "Weybridge and Shepperton"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 12. At dawn the narrator and the artilleryman creep out along a road strewn with what people dropped as they ran: a clock, a slipper, a silver spoon. Through the hushed pine woods they hail three hussars, and nobody believes them about giants a hundred feet high.

Weybridge is in a tumult, the town packing in its Sunday best, and one old fellow will not leave his orchids. By noon they reach Shepperton, where the Wey meets the Thames, with too few boats for the crowd. Then a gun thuds towards Chertsey, and one, two, three, four fighting machines come striding across the meadows to the river.

The narrator runs headlong into the water. The six hidden guns at Shepperton fire together, a shell bursts clean in a Martian's face, and the headless machine reels on, strikes down the church tower, and falls.

Chapter XII of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "What I Saw of the Destruction of Weybridge and Shepperton", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
